defects.source_says: The held text (5 FR 5143, FR issue of December 18, 1940) closes the agencies 'all day on Tuesday, December 24,1940'; the order was signed December 16, 1940. The end by own terms is 1940-12-24, and a 1937 end precedes the order's own signing; the claim's own judgment_reason and research_rationale say December 24, 1940.
Publication was in the Federal Register issue of Wednesday, December 18, 1940 (filed December 17, 1940); the judgment_reason itself says December 18, 1940.
Latest clause end on the sources is December 24, 1940; the recorded date is three years wrong and earlier than the order's signing date 1940-12-16, contradicting the research_rationale.

reasoning: Hashes and quoted spans are exact; identity (No. 8613, signed December 16, 1940, Roosevelt, 'Excusing Federal Employees From Duty on December 24, 1940', 5 FR 5143, FR Doc. 40-5680) agrees with the held text and the OFR catalog record (empty disposition note). The two-paragraph inventory is complete, the own-terms reasoning, savings and searches are sound, and no earlier end or later event exists in held texts (cruden 0 hits; catalog, U.S. Code and eCFR searches 0 hits). But every structured end date is 1937 instead of 1940: clause 1 and whole_order_end give 1937-12-24 and clause 2 gives 1937-12-18, dates before the order existed and inconsistent with the claim's own judgment_reason and rationale. Structured dates are what enter the ledger, so the claim is rejected despite correct reasoning; corrected values would be 1940-12-24, 1940-12-18 and whole_order_end 1940-12-24.

The whole order is one revocation under section 1 of the Act of August 1, 1914 plus the effective-date sentence, so a single clause is a complete inventory. Savings: loss of port status is a surviving effect of an executed act, no savings clause. whole_order_end equals the sole clause end. The working text is FR OCR, page images not inspected, as disclosed.
